summary: Fixed one description drift issue for daily_revenue.

findings.claim: The effective catalog description claimed revenue includes all orders, but the SQL includes only completed orders.

evidence.fact: Before remediation, the description override stated: Revenue from all orders at one row per order date.
SQL filters status = 'completed', sums amount, and groups by order_date.

evidence.source: python -c "import re,pathlib; s=pathlib.Path('project/models/daily_revenue.sql').read_text(); assert re.search(r\"where\\s+status\\s*=\\s*'completed'\",s); assert re.search(r'group\\s+by\\s+order_date',s); print('PASS: parsed SQL filters completed orders and groups by order_date')"
evidence.fact: SQL parsing checks confirmed the completed-status filter and order_date grouping.
The model description explicitly states completed-order revenue excludes refunded and cancelled orders.
The daily_revenue model description matches the schema documentation and corrected catalog description.

action.value: Completed-order revenue at one row per order date; refunded and cancelled orders are excluded.
action.rationale: Replace the stale override with the directly supported dbt description.

verification.equals: Completed-order revenue at one row per order date; refunded and cancelled orders are excluded.

changes_made.description: Corrected daily_revenue.description to reflect the completed-order filter.
